{{Short description|Extension of a transitive set}}
In [[model theory]] and [[set theory]], a model <math>\mathfrak{B}=\langle B, F\rangle </math> of some axiom system of [[set theory]] <math> T</math> in the language of set theory is an '''end extension''' of <math>\mathfrak{A}=\langle A, E\rangle </math>, in symbols <math>\mathfrak{A}\subseteq_\text{end}\mathfrak{B}</math>, if 
# <math>\mathfrak{A}</math> is a [[substructure (mathematics)|substructure]] of <math>\mathfrak{B}</math>, (i.e.,  <math>A \subseteq B</math> and <math>E = F|_A</math>), and 
# <math> b\in A</math> whenever <math>a\in A</math> and <math>bFa</math> hold, i.e., no new elements are added by <math>\mathfrak{B}</math> to the elements of <math>A</math>.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Keisler |first1=H. Jerome |author1-link=Howard Jerome Keisler |last2=Silver |first2=Jack H. |author2-link=Jack Silver |chapter=End extensions of models of set theory |pages=177–187 |title=Axiomatic Set Theory |year=1971 |series=Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics |volume=13, Part 1 |editor-last=Scott |editor-first=Dana |editor-link=Dana Scott |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |location=[[Providence, Rhode Island|Providence, RI]] |isbn=0-8218-0245-3 |mr=0321729}}</ref>

The second condition can be equivalently written as <math>\{b\in A : b E a\}=\{b\in B : b F a\}</math> for all <math>a\in A</math>.

For example, <math>\langle B, \in\rangle </math> is an end extension of <math>\langle A, \in\rangle </math> if <math> A</math> and <math>B</math> are [[transitive set]]s, and  <math> A\subseteq B</math>.

A related concept is that of a '''top extension''' (also known as rank extension), where a model <math>\mathfrak{B}=\langle B, F\rangle </math> is a top extension of a model <math>\mathfrak{A}=\langle A, E\rangle </math> if <math>\mathfrak{A}\subseteq_\text{end}\mathfrak{B}</math> and for all <math>a \in A</math> and <math> b \in B\setminus A</math>, we have <math>\operatorname{rank}(b) > \operatorname{rank}(a)</math>, where <math>\operatorname{rank}(\cdot)</math> denotes the [[Rank_(set_theory)|rank]] of a set.

==Existence==

[[Howard Jerome Keisler|Keisler]] and [[Michael D. Morley|Morley]] showed that every countable model of ZF has an end extension which is also an [[elementary substructure|elementary extension]].<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Keisler | first1=H. Jerome 
| author1-link=Howard Jerome Keisler
| last2=Morley | first2=Michael
| author2-link=Michael D. Morley
| title=Elementary extensions of models of set theory
| journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]
| volume=6
| issue=1
| date=1968
| pages=49–65
| doi=10.1007/BF02771605}}</ref> If the elementarity requirement is weakened to being elementary for formulae that are <math>\Sigma_n</math> on the [[Lévy hierarchy]], every countable structure in which <math>\Sigma_n</math>-collection holds has a <math>\Sigma_n</math>-elementary end extension.<ref>{{cite book
| last1=Kaufmann | first1=Matt
| chapter=On existence of Σ<sub>''n''</sub> end extensions
| series=[[Lecture Notes in Mathematics]]
| volume=859
| title=Logic Year 1979–80: University of Connecticut, USA
| date=1981
| publisher=[[Springer-Verlag|Springer]]
| location=[[Berlin]], [[Heidelberg]]
| pages=92–103
| isbn=978-3-540-10708-8
| doi=10.1007/BFb0090942
| editor1-last=Lerman |editor1-first=M.
